# `m.reference.market_holidays`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The upcoming market holidays and early closes, one row per exchange and day.

```python
m.reference.market_holidays()
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Exchange` and `Date` (`dm.PollMode.REPLACE`) |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Open` | Instant | The market open time on the holiday (if it's not closed). | REST |
| `Date` | String | The date of the holiday. | REST |
| `Close` | Instant | The market close time on the holiday (if it's not closed). | REST |
| `Exchange` | String | Which market the record is for. | REST |
| `Name` | String | The name of the holiday. | REST |
| `Status` | String | The status of the market on the holiday. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
